key_insight: Bulk second-gradient elasticity enables minimizer existence under broad surface-energy assumptions while introducing a length scale that delays elastocapillary beading and favors longer wavelengths.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps predict instability onset and beaded morphologies in stretched soft cylinders where surface energy and bulk length-scale effects interact.
method: Prove minimizer existence under suitable bulk coercivity and second-gradient convexity assumptions.
Derive a finite-strain, small-on-large incremental formulation for cylinder stability.
Implement C1-continuous isogeometric analysis in OOFEM and trace post-bifurcation branches by arc-length continuation.
evidence_signal: Finite-cylinder simulations show onset stretches in close agreement with analytical predictions; selected branches shift from supercritical beading at small second-gradient moduli to subcritical thick–thin segmentation at larger moduli.
watch_item: Instability trends are reported for the parameters studied, and implementation requires C1-continuous discretizations.
paper_title: Finite-strain second-gradient elasticity with an energetic surface: existence of minimizers, incremental theory and elastocapillary beading
